title: Best Children's Book Illustrators (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a children's book illustrator: what the package should include, how to brief it, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: A children's picture book lives or dies by its illustrations. The illustrator must create characters that stay consistent across every page, leave room for text, and deliver files your printer or publishing platform accepts. Projects go wrong when page layouts are not planned, rights are unclear, or AI-generated images are sold as hand-made. This guide helps you plan a smooth project.

faq.q: How many illustrations does a picture book need?
faq.a: It depends on the page count and layout. Many picture books have an illustration on every spread. Plan the page count with your printer or publishing platform first.

faq.q: Should I send the full story?
faq.a: Yes, with a page-by-page breakdown of which text goes where. The illustrator needs to plan the flow and leave space for text.
It varies. Some illustrators transfer full rights; others license them for the book only, with extra fees for merchandise or adaptations. Agree in writing before starting.

faq.q: Does the illustrator also do the layout?
faq.a: Sometimes. Layout, text placement and the cover are often separate. Ask what is included and who prepares the final print files.
Ask directly. If you want hand-made art or need clear copyright, confirm how the illustrations are made.
